target.title: fix(google-meet): bound Calendar v3 events.list request deadline
target.body:
## Summary

- add `timeoutMs` to the single `fetchWithSsrFGuard` call in `extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.ts` (the Calendar v3 `events.list` URL) so the calendar-driven gateway flows (`findGoogleMeetCalendarEvent` → `listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents` → `fetchGoogleCalendarEvents`) get a bounded request deadline
- plumb `timeoutMs?` through the internal `fetchGoogleCalendarEvents` helper and the two exported wrappers `listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents` and `findGoogleMeetCalendarEvent` so callers can override the default
- default to `GOOGLE_CALENDAR_DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000` — matches Alix-007's pattern in #102050 (Google Vertex ADC) and the 30s convention across the active HTTP-timeout campaign
- add a new `extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.test.ts` that drives a real `node:http` loopback hanging server via the production `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → `globalThis.fetch` path (with the production `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` AbortSignal attached to `init.signal`) and asserts (a) no `timeoutMs` stays pending against the hanging server, and (b) `timeoutMs: 50` rejects with an `abort|timeout` error after the deadline fires — two `it()` cases (one per behavior), reusing the same `startHangingCalendarServer` fixture
- mutation test verified: removing the new `timeoutMs: params.timeoutMs ?? GOOGLE_CALENDAR_DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` line from `fetchGoogleCalendarEvents` makes the `timeoutMs: 50` reject case fail with `expected timeout rejection, got pending`; restoring the line returns 2/2 tests to green
- this PR complements #102149 (google-meet Meet v2 + Drive files.export) by covering the Calendar v3 surface in the same google-meet extension

## Why this change is needed

`fetchGoogleCalendarEvents` (extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.ts:158) is the single internal helper that backs both `listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents` and `findGoogleMeetCalendarEvent`, and it calls `fetchWithSsrFGuard` against `https://www.googleapis.com/calendar/v3/calendars/{id}/events` without a request deadline. The guarded fetch returns a real `Response` only when the upstream Calendar v3 endpoint responds; if the Google network accepts the request but never sends headers (TCP half-open, captive portal, gateway-side firewall reset, GFE stall), the helper sits on the `await fetchWithSsrFGuard(...)` indefinitely and the gateway's calendar-driven flows (the CLI `codex meet ...` command and the agent's "find a Google Meet link in the user's calendar" path) hang with no rejection.

`fetchWithSsrFGuard` already accepts a `timeoutMs` option and runs `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` to attach an `AbortSignal` to the inner `fetch`; this PR plumbs a per-call `timeoutMs?` through the Calendar helper chain and defaults to 30s when the caller does not override it.

This is the same pattern Alix-007 used in #102050 (Google Vertex ADC token refresh, OPEN, 🐚 ready for maintainer look) and the broader HTTP-timeout campaign wave (Alix-007 #102026 chutes / #102027 mattermost / #102028 qqbot / #102025 nextcloud-talk / #102050 google Vertex — all 6/8 channels opened 2026-07-08). It is the Calendar-side complement to #102149 (Meet v2 + Drive files.export) in the same google-meet extension.

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.test.ts` — passed; 1 file, 2 tests
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/google-meet/` — passed; 17 files, 196 tests (no regressions; +2 from this PR)
- PR diff: 2 files, +194/-0 (calendar.ts 5+0, calendar.test.ts 189+0)
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.ts extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.test.ts` — all files correctly formatted
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.ts extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.test.ts` — no findings
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` — passed
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` — passed (the test-typecheck gap that #98322 caught is not bypassed)
- mutation check: removing the new `timeoutMs: params.timeoutMs ?? GOOGLE_CALENDAR_DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` line from `fetchGoogleCalendarEvents` makes the `listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents rejects with an abort|timeout error when timeoutMs: 50 fires` test fail with `expected timeout rejection, got pending`; restoring the line returns 2/2 tests to green. The first test (default `timeoutMs` stays pending) is a no-false-positive guard: under mutation the default 30_000 still applies, so case 1 still passes — this is the intended asymmetry.

## Evidence

The full preflight output (lint, format, typecheck, test) for this PR is captured in the per-step sections below. The decisive evidence is in [## Real behavior proof](#real-behavior-proof) — the real `node:http` loopback server hanging the request and the `buildTimeoutAbortSignal`-attached `AbortSignal` aborting the inner `fetch` after the deadline fires.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: `fetchGoogleCalendarEvents` in `extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.ts` (reached via `listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents` and `findGoogleMeetCalendarEvent`) now rejects with an error whose `name` matches `/abort|timeout/i` after the requested `timeoutMs` elapses, instead of hanging indefinitely on a half-open TCP connection to `https://www.googleapis.com/calendar/v3/calendars/{id}/events`.

**Real environment tested**: local Linux Node 22.22 source checkout. The new `extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.test.ts` stands up a real `node:http` server bound to `127.0.0.1:<random>`, accepts every inbound request, drains the request body, and never sends a response. The test replaces `globalThis.fetch` with a `vi.stubGlobal("fetch", vi.fn(...))` that rewrites the production `https://www.googleapis.com/calendar/v3/...` URL host to the loopback origin and forwards the production `init` (which already carries the `AbortSignal` that `fetchWithSsrFGuard` attached via `buildTimeoutAbortSignal({ timeoutMs, operation: "fetchWithSsrFGuard", url })`) to a captured handle of the real `fetch`. The production guarded-fetch path runs end-to-end: `listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents` → `fetchGoogleCalendarEvents` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` → `fetchWithRuntimeDispatcher` → mocked `globalThis.fetch` → loopback `fetch` → hanging `node:http` socket.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.test.ts --reporter=verbose` — 2/2 tests pass; the 2 verbose test names are:
  - `Google Calendar v3 request timeouts > listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents stays pending against a hanging Calendar v3 endpoint when no timeoutMs is passed` (~410 ms)
  - `Google Calendar v3 request timeouts > listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents rejects with an abort|timeout error when timeoutMs: 50 fires against a hanging Calendar v3 endpoint` (~60 ms)

**Evidence after fix** (output of the verbose test run):
```
✓ |extensions| extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.test.ts > Google Calendar v3 request timeouts > listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents stays pending against a hanging Calendar v3 endpoint when no timeoutMs is passed 408ms
✓ |extensions| extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.test.ts > Google Calendar v3 request timeouts > listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents rejects with an abort|timeout error when timeoutMs: 50 fires against a hanging Calendar v3 endpoint 60ms

Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  2 passed (2)
```

The first test (no-`timeoutMs` default-pending) asserts, in order:
1. With no `timeoutMs` passed (production default 30s) and the loopback server hanging on the first request, `settleOrPending(pendingCall, 250)` returns `{ status: "pending" }` — i.e. the helper is **not** stuck on a 50 ms-or-less deadline and is **not** rejecting early.

The second test (`timeoutMs: 50` reject) asserts, in order:
1. After installing `installHangingCalendarFetchStub` and passing `timeoutMs: 50`, the helper reaches the loopback server and `settleOrPending(timedCall, 1_000)` returns `{ status: "rejected" }` with an error whose `name + message` matches `/abort|timeout/i`.

**Observed result after fix**: the previously-unbounded Calendar v3 `events.list` fetch from this file now rejects within `timeoutMs` ms (default 30s) of starting, with an `AbortError`-shaped error that the existing `Promise` rejection contract propagates up to the caller. The existing public function signatures are preserved — `listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents` and `findGoogleMeetCalendarEvent` each grow a new optional `timeoutMs?: number` field that defaults to 30s when omitted, so existing call sites in `extensions/google-meet/src/cli.ts:694` (findGoogleMeetCalendarEvent) and `extensions/google-meet/src/cli.ts:1936` (listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents) compile and run unchanged.

**What was not tested**: a real OS-level EPIPE or TCP RST against a live Calendar v3 endpoint. The regression test exercises the simpler `AbortSignal` contract directly through a real `node:http` loopback server, which is the same shape the Alix-007 #102050 (Google Vertex ADC) test uses for the canonical HTTP-timeout pattern. The `findGoogleMeetCalendarEvent` wrapper is exercised by the same test via the fact that `findGoogleMeetCalendarEvent` calls `listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents` (calendar.ts:245), and the inner `fetchGoogleCalendarEvents` call is the only `fetchWithSsrFGuard` site in the file, so a single regression test on `listGoogleMeetCalendarEvents` covers the entire chain.

## Campaign coordination

This PR is part of the active HTTP request timeout campaign wave in 2026-07:

- OPEN: #102050 (google vertex ADC, Alix-007, 🐚), #102028 (qqbot speech, Alix-007, 🐚), #102027 (mattermost REST, Alix-007, 🐚), #102026 (chutes OAuth, Alix-007, 🐚), #102025 (nextcloud-talk Talk, Alix-007, 🐚), #101649 (zalouser probe, Alix-007, 🐚), #102094 (dashscope video, Alix-007, 🐚), #102072 (minimax media, Alix-007, 🐚), #102062 (openrouter video, Alix-007, 🐚), #102089 (twilio redact, Alix-007, 🦞), #102149 (google-meet Meet v2 + Drive files.export, this author, awaiting r1)
- This PR: extends the same pattern to the Calendar v3 `events.list` site in the google-meet extension; complements #102149 (Meet v2 + Drive files.export) on the same extension.

**Collision check**: no open PR touches the Google Meet Calendar v3 surface (`extensions/google-meet/src/calendar.ts`) for HTTP timeouts. Verified via `gh search prs "google-meet calendar timeout" --repo openclaw/openclaw --state all` and `gh pr list --state all --search "google-meet calendar" --json number,title,state,author`; the only historical closed PRs on the surface are bounded-read fixes (OOM prevention, see #97783 Alix-007 CLOSED, #97832 cxbAsDev CLOSED, #97879 cxbAsDev CLOSED, #98355 lsr911 CLOSED) — those are a different fix shape (response body cap, not request deadline) and the closed verdicts were stale-review rebase issues, not the bounded-read fix being wrong. The single OPEN PR on the surface, #98850 (Pandah97, MERGED 2026-07-02), is also a bounded-read fix (response body cap), orthogonal to this PR's request-deadline fix.
